packs.title: Civic Lines & Garden Paths
packs.promise: Read Buenos Aires through a civic square, a working theater, a Subte journey and northern gardens.

q.s: Give Puente de la Mujer an original three-line portrait.
st: At the open Dique 3 promenade, find a permitted view of Puente de la Mujer with its angled mast and tension cables visible.
If the pedestrian crossing is open, walk it normally and stop only in a suitable place clear of passing people. Otherwise remain on the open dockside.
Create three lines in words or drawing: one for the mast’s direction, one for the cables and one for the water’s horizontal surface.
Add a title of your own. Let the lines describe your observation without claiming to explain the architect’s intentions.

q.s: Read plant labels, then compare what grows above them.
st: On an open Tuesday–Friday afternoon, enter the Botánico through a public visitor entrance. Entry is listed free; check weather and date closures before travelling.
Choose three labelled plants visible from open paths. Copy each name as the label gives it, leaving illegible words uncertain.
For each plant, record one visible feature: leaf shape, stem texture or growth form. Compare the feature rather than guessing a survival purpose.
Write one question about why those forms differ. You may use a public interpretation panel for an answer only if it addresses the question directly.

q.t: A Flower Made of City Light
q.s: Make an original palette from Floralis Genérica’s reflective surfaces.
st: From an open public path, find a permitted view of the metal flower Floralis Genérica. Keep behind any water or maintenance boundary.
Choose three tones you actually see in the metal and surroundings. In words or drawing, arrange them into a small palette that follows the sculpture’s curves.
Give each tone your own descriptive name and write which real surface or reflection supplied it.
Finish with a two-sentence portrait of the flower as it appears now. Do not wait for the petals to move or claim that the mechanism is operating.

packs.title: San Telmo in Detail
packs.promise: Follow San Telmo from a comic-strip corner to market ironwork, museum rooms and a park monument.

q.s: Give one ordinary San Telmo moment three frames of your own.
st: At the Chile and Defensa corner, find a public-pavement position from which you can see the Mafalda statue without joining or blocking a photo queue.
Watch one ordinary street action unfold: someone carrying a parcel, a door opening or a changing patch of light. Choose an action that respects strangers’ privacy.
Draw three small frames showing before, during and after, or write three short scene descriptions. Make the sequence yours; do not copy Quino’s dialogue or put words in his characters’ mouths.
Give your sequence a title, then point out the detail that places it at this corner rather than an imaginary street.

q.s: Collect the structures that keep San Telmo’s market light.
st: During the market’s published 09:00–20:00 opening, enter through an open public visitor entrance and remain in the ordinary aisles. Follow staff instructions.
Look above the stalls for one metal support, one curved structural element and one area where daylight comes through the roof.
Trace how your three observations connect: what carries weight, what spans a gap and what admits light? Describe what you can see without claiming an engineering calculation.
Add one present-day market activity beneath that roof. Do not handle stock or require a vendor to take part.

q.s: Turn a museum encounter into an original visual or written reply.
st: On an open Wednesday–Friday afternoon, obtain the required Museo Moderno admission before entering. Wednesday is listed without charge; confirm the date and current ticket conditions.
Choose one work in an open gallery that holds your attention. Record its title and maker only as given by the museum; do not invent an attribution.
Write three words for what you notice in its materials, shapes or arrangement. Then create your own small response: a line drawing or a four-sentence scene using those observations.
Finish with one question about the work. Keep your response and interpretation separate from facts supplied by its label.
